# Pinmux RTL Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The pinmux module provides programmable routing and configuration between peripheral I/O signals and chip pads. It supports a configurable number of muxed bidirectional pads and a configurable number of dedicated pads. The module controls pad signal selection, pad electrical attributes, sleep-state retention, wakeup detection, strap sampling, JTAG signal qualification, and USB wake detection.

The module is programmable through a memory-mapped register interface. All configuration and status information is accessed through this interface. After reset, the module must be in a fully deterministic state: all pad outputs and output enables must be known, all pad attributes must be at their reset values, all muxed pad outputs must be in a high-impedance state, and all peripheral inputs must be at their default reset value.

## 2. Pad Groups and Signal Routing

### 2.1 Muxed Pads

Muxed pads are bidirectional pads whose data, output enable, and input routing are software-configurable.

- Each peripheral input can select its source from:
  - constant 0
  - constant 1
  - any of the muxed pad inputs
- The selection is controlled by a per-input select register.
- After reset, all peripheral inputs must be tied to constant 0 unless a design-specific override is provided.

### 2.2 Muxed Pad Outputs

Each muxed pad has a combined output data and output enable selection. The pad must be driveable to one of the following states:

- Drive constant 0
- Drive constant 1
- High-impedance (output enable off)
- Drive a selected peripheral output data and output enable pair

The output select is controlled by a per-pad register. After reset, all muxed pads must be in the high-impedance state.

### 2.3 Dedicated Pads

Dedicated pads are owned by a specific peripheral and are not muxed.

- The input of a dedicated pad must be routed directly to its corresponding peripheral input.
- The output data and output enable of a dedicated pad must be taken directly from the corresponding peripheral output signals.
- Dedicated pads still support pad attribute configuration, sleep retention, and wakeup detection.

## 3. Pad Attribute Configuration

Each muxed pad and each dedicated pad has a programmable pad attribute register. The register controls electrical pad properties such as inversion, pull-up, pull-down, open-drain, keeper, drive strength, and slew rate, where supported.

- The module must apply a legality mask to each pad attribute register based on the physical pad type.
- Unsupported or illegal attribute bits must be forced to their legal values when written.
- The masked attribute value must be continuously applied to the pad.
- Reads of the attribute register must return the masked/legalized value, not the raw written value.

## 4. Sleep Retention Behavior

The module supports a low-power sleep mode in which selected pads hold a configured output state.

When the sleep enable input transitions from inactive to active, the module must:

1. Check each pad’s sleep enable bit.
2. For pads with sleep enabled, capture the pad output data and output enable according to that pad’s configured sleep mode:
   - Drive low: output data low, output enable on
   - Drive high: output data high, output enable on
   - High-impedance: output enable off
   - Hold previous value: retain the current output data and output enable values
3. Set the sleep status bit for each pad whose output is captured.

While a pad’s sleep status bit is set, the pad output data and output enable must come from the captured retention state instead of the normal mux/direct connection. The sleep status bit must remain set until cleared by software or reset.

Both muxed and dedicated pads must support this behavior.

## 5. Wakeup Detectors

The module provides multiple independent wakeup detector channels. Each channel monitors a selected chip pad input and may generate a wakeup request.

Each detector channel must support:

- Selection of a pad from either the muxed or dedicated pad group
- Enable/disable control
- Configurable filtering and debounce behavior
- A programmable event mode (such as edge or level detection)
- A counter threshold for qualifying the event

When a qualified event is detected on an enabled channel, the channel must:

- Generate a wakeup request
- Update its wakeup cause status so software can read which channel caused the wakeup
- The wakeup cause must be clearable by software

All wakeup requests must be combined into a single wakeup request output. The wakeup detector logic must operate in the always-on clock domain, allowing wakeup requests to be generated during low-power states.

## 6. Strap Sampling and JTAG Signal Handling

The module is responsible for sampling chip strap values and for qualifying JTAG signals. The behavior is controlled by strap enable, lifecycle DFT/debug enables, scan mode, and a DFT hold signal.

### 6.1 Strap Sampling

- When strap sampling is enabled, the module must capture the current values of the relevant pads and present them as a sampled strap output.
- The sampled strap values must be held stable while strap sampling is active.
- When the DFT hold signal is asserted, the module must stop updating the sample and hold the last captured values.
- The sampled strap output must be in a known state after reset.

### 6.2 JTAG Signal Qualification

The module must provide qualified JTAG signals to multiple internal TAP destinations. The routing and qualification are controlled by the lifecycle DFT enable and hardware debug enable inputs.

- JTAG signals presented to each destination must be deterministic and known after reset.
- The module must support up to three TAP destinations, with selection behavior determined by the lifecycle and DFT control inputs.
- Scan mode may alter strap sampling and JTAG qualification behavior to support scan testing.

## 7. USB Wake Detection

The module includes USB wake detection logic. This function monitors dedicated pads associated with USB data lines and USB pull-up enables.

The USB wake detection must:

- Operate in the always-on clock domain.
- Accept inputs indicating whether the USB device is out of reset, enabled for wake, suspended, and wake-acknowledged.
- Monitor the USB data pad input states and the output enables of the USB pull-up pads.
- When the system is in a low-power state and a USB resume/wake condition is detected, assert a USB wake request output.
- Provide a debug output that reflects the internal USB wake detection state.

The USB wake request must only be asserted when the appropriate enable conditions are satisfied.

## 8. Register Interface

The module must provide a memory-mapped slave interface for all configuration, status, and control registers.

- All registers must be initialized to their reset values after reset.
- Writes to read-only fields must have no effect.
- Writes to WARL fields must be legalized according to the field/pad type, and reads must return the legalized values.
- Software must be able to read current pad output status, sleep status, and wakeup cause status.
- The module must not allow invalid pad routing selections to cause unknown or indeterminate output states. All selectors must be bounded by the available pad and peripheral signal counts.

# Pinmux Strap Sampling Module Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is the chip-boundary front-end for boot-strap capture and JTAG TAP selection. It performs the following functions:

- Samples configured strap pins into internal storage.
- Provides the sampled DFT strap value and a sticky valid indication.
- Selects one of three JTAG TAPs based on the sampled TAP-select straps.
- Qualifies RISC-V and DFT TAP access using life-cycle enable controls.
- Drives the physical JTAG pads only when a TAP is actively selected.
- Passes all non-JTAG pads through unchanged between the core side and the physical pad side.

The design-time target configuration defines which physical pads carry the two TAP-select straps, the two DFT straps, and the JTAG signals.

## 2. Reset Behavior

When the module reset is asserted, the module shall:

- Clear the sampled DFT strap value to zero.
- Deassert the DFT strap valid output.
- Initialize the TAP-select storage to the value that selects the life-cycle TAP.

After reset, the life-cycle TAP is therefore the default JTAG TAP until a TAP-select strap is sampled to a different value.

## 3. Strap Sampling

The module samples a set of strap values from physical pads:

- Two TAP-select strap values.
- Two DFT strap values.

Sampling occurs when either of the following is true:

1. The strap-sample pulse input is asserted.
2. Continuous DFT sampling mode is active.

The strap-sample pulse is expected to be asserted once after cold boot. While it is high, the module samples the strap pins on each clock edge.

Continuous DFT sampling mode is active when the DFT life-cycle enable is on and the hold-TAP-select control is not asserted. While this mode is active, the module continuously samples all strap values. The hold-TAP-select control disables continuous sampling; it does not prevent a direct strap-sample pulse from sampling.

While a sampling condition is active, the following rules apply:

- The life-cycle TAP-select strap is sampled unconditionally.
- The RISC-V TAP-select strap is sampled only when the hardware debug life-cycle enable is on.
- The DFT straps are sampled only when the DFT life-cycle enable is on.

When no sampling condition is active, the stored strap values shall remain unchanged.

## 4. DFT Strap Output

The DFT strap output is valid only when the sticky valid indication is asserted.

After reset, the DFT valid indication is deasserted. Once the DFT straps have been sampled while the DFT sampling condition is active, the valid indication shall assert and shall remain asserted until reset. It shall not be cleared by later changes to the DFT life-cycle enable or by disabling sampling.

The DFT strap output value shall reflect the most recently sampled DFT strap bits.

## 5. JTAG TAP Selection

The module connects the JTAG path to one of three TAPs:

- The life-cycle TAP.
- The RISC-V TAP.
- The DFT TAP.

The sampled TAP-select straps determine which TAP is requested:

- If the TAP-select straps select the life-cycle TAP, that TAP is selected unconditionally.
- If they select the RISC-V TAP, that TAP is selected only when the hardware debug life-cycle enable is on.
- If they select the DFT TAP, that TAP is selected only when the DFT life-cycle enable is on.
- If they select a TAP whose life-cycle enable is off, or if the sampled value is not a defined TAP selection, no TAP is selected.

When a TAP is selected, the module shall:

- Forward the JTAG inputs to that TAP.
- Forward that TAP’s test-data output and output-enable to the physical test-data-output pad.
- Hold all non-selected TAPs in reset and ignore their outputs.

When no TAP is selected, all TAPs shall be held in reset, no TAP shall receive JTAG activity, and the JTAG pads shall not be taken over by the module.

## 6. JTAG Pad Behavior

When a TAP is selected, the module takes over the configured JTAG pads. In this JTAG-active mode:

- The JTAG pad inputs are not forwarded to the core side; the corresponding core input values are forced low.
- The test-data-output pad is driven by the selected TAP’s test-data output and output-enable. If that output-enable is low, the pad is high-impedance.
- The other JTAG pads are placed in a non-driving state so the module does not contend with the external JTAG driver.
- Pad attributes for all JTAG pads are forced to their inactive/default values.

When no TAP is selected, or for all non-JTAG pads, the module shall pass the pad interface through unchanged:

- Pad inputs drive the core-side input values.
- Core-side output data drives the pad output data.
- Core-side output-enable drives the pad output-enable.
- Core-side pad attributes drive the pad attributes.

## 7. JTAG Reset Behavior

The JTAG test reset delivered to the selected TAP depends on scan mode:

- When scan mode is not active, the external test-reset pin is used.
- When scan mode is active, the module’s own reset is used instead, and the external test-reset pin is ignored.

The same JTAG reset behavior applies regardless of which TAP is currently selected.
